inputs.original_text: A Fianna Fáil TD has called for reform of inheritance tax exemption thresholds, describing the current system as ‘wholly unfair’ and discriminatory against those without children. John Lahart’s comments follow recent contributions from party colleagues on the need to review how inheritance tax is applied across different family structures. inputs.modified_text: John Lahart is right that people without children shouldn’t be treated as less deserving under inheritance tax rules. But equal treatment across family structures is only part of the picture: inheritance allows wealth and advantage to accumulate across generations, while everyone else is left to contend with unequal opportunities. Reform should protect people from discrimination without expanding the ability of the wealthy to preserve privilege, and it must not put private inheritance ahead of the public resources we all rely on.
